independenceMethod: After publishing the repair, freshly retrieved both controlling OER PDFs and verified their exact hashes. Reopened their outcomes, course/credit tables and admission/choice rules, and actual workbook profiles/descriptions for the strongest ancient-world, textual, historical and philosophical candidates. Reconsidered the no-match and finished audience content from these underlying sources rather than the author summary. Same AI as author, not an independent person or another model; runtime model/effort unknown.
academicChallenges: The adopted Dutch-language Radboud Classics programme has twelve first-year 5-EC units, six second-year 5-EC units plus 30 EC of fixed Humanities minors, and four final-year 5-EC units plus a 10-EC thesis and 30 EC of open study. This is 180 EC in 25 positions. Required mentorship, academic Dutch assessment, second-year personal development and thesis colloquium do not add credits. Ordinary domestic study with both school languages is a neutral valid pathway; alternative exchange/education substitutions are not mixed into it.

Grammar intensification replaces the relevant first texts course after grammar 1 or 2. Later literature/linguistics/epigraphy requires the appropriate Greek/Latin grammar, and the thesis requires both named literary/cultural methods courses. These requirements can be met within the preceding years. The two 15-EC Arts minors have fixed packages, and other-faculty minors belong only in open space. Open study is bachelor-level study outside the own programme; foreign study requires advance approval. The prospective future-year tables do not override the adopted 2026–27 OER.

All 42 exact-target interests were revisited. Thirteen eligible rows were assigned to the closest text/culture attempt, reception/rhetoric or classical-language education. Fourteen topics supply support, two illustrations and thirteen outcomes remain discovery only. The official after-study page explicitly includes Dutch as a Second Language and Communication and Information Studies as master pathways; their surprising presence is not evidence of compulsory BA content or UCR provision. Digital tools remain a limited curricular lead, without an invented required digital Classics unit.

Current UCR Greek Archaeology and Heritage & Ancient Democracy genuinely examine ancient Greek material culture and citizenship. World Archaeology offers artefact/craft inquiry across ancient societies. World Myth & Literature gives Greek/Roman comparative narratives and Ovidian retelling; Rhetorical Communication teaches Greek and Roman rhetorical traditions. Great Literary Works, Western/Political Philosophy, History of Empires and Ways of War contribute actual ancient material within broader scope. These are fully counted as academic contributions, including description-only courses. Generic literary criticism, stylistics and art historiography also supply genuine methods; their objects and methods are not silently relabelled as source-language philology.

Two full 24-course candidate palettes were challenged across 28 actual course records. The first combines the strongest ancient material with literary/visual interpretation and reception; the second prioritises ancient democracy and subsequent political thought. The necessary general and modern courses shift the organising academic object away from sustained Greek/Roman textual, historical and material inquiry. The rejected judgement concerns the full programme, not the absence of the degree title, language training alone, a prescribed number of ancient courses or demand for equivalence. The teaching direction was considered separately: real primary-school rhetorical teaching practice does not establish a classical-language education curriculum. No defensible first alternative was established, so no accepted UCR schedule or comparison rows are manufactured.

All 25 English component titles agree with the adopted Dutch requirements and credits. Reader-facing programme and no-match explanations, route/year/status limits, component notes, source links and audience references were read under the established field-to-renderer mapping. Original research/sourceNotes remain internal. The exception displays the supported external curriculum and no UCR programme, concepts, optional research or course-description modals. Candidate workbook content was nevertheless reviewed substantively. No app code, Shiny, browser, screenshots or live modals were used. Case content approval grants no runtime or final release approval.
scope: All six stages, complete 180-EC external pathway, all 42 interests, strongest actual UCR candidate content and complete exception audience record. No approved UCR programme/schedule exists; its schedule and selected modal checks are inapplicable, not failed. Final release remains separately unauthorised.
